title: All 57-pair disjoint sets retained a larger-first majority in deep ComCat earthquakes in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether pair choice can reverse the observed larger-first majority in deep ComCat earthquakes in 2000-2025. Both events had depth greater than 300 km and preferred magnitude at least 5.5. Pairs had positive lags through seven days, hypocenter distances through 200 km and magnitude gaps of at least 0.3. The catalog had 81 larger-first cases among 112 eligible pairs. We computed exact bounds over all largest disjoint pair sets, so each event could enter only once. The largest sets had 57 pairs. Their larger-first counts ranged from 39 to 45, or 68.4% to 78.9%. Thus every such set retained a majority. All eight planned rule checks also had lower bounds above 50%. A separate scalar-geometry audit and exhaustive enumeration of all primary graph components reproduced the bounds. These are deterministic bounds for a fixed revised catalog, not confidence limits or proof of triggering. Smaller pair sets, catalog error and physical detection effects are not bounded. This method audit uses data that overlap prior campaign work. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure and source provenance are included; external event records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Exact range of larger-first shares over all largest disjoint pair sets. Orange points show all-pair shares. Ranges are not confidence intervals.
